slides.title: Understanding Dunder Methods in Python
slides.prompt: Magic methods (or dunder methods) are special methods with double underscores like __init__ or __str__. They allow custom classes to emulate built-in types and define custom behaviors for operators.

slides.title: String Representation
slides.prompt: Fill in the magic method name used to return an official, unambiguous string representation of an object (often used for debugging).

slides.title: Operator Overloading for Addition
slides.prompt: Which dunder method must be implemented to customize the behavior of the '+' operator for a class?

slides.title: Custom Length Implementation
slides.prompt: Fill in the dunder method used to support the built-in len() function on custom objects.

slides.title: Callable Instances
slides.prompt: Which dunder method allows an instance of a class to be called like a function (e.g., obj())?

slides.title: Equality Comparison
slides.prompt: Fill in the magic method used to evaluate equality using the '==' operator.

slides.title: Attribute Access Control
slides.prompt: Which magic method is invoked automatically when an attribute lookup is NOT found in the instance dictionary?
